title: Japan and China: Trying to Be Friends Again
summary:
Have you ever had a big fight with a friend and then tried to make up? That's what's happening between Japan and China. Japanese lawmakers flew to Beijing on Monday to try to fix their relationship.

The trouble started when Japan's Prime Minister, Sanae Takaichi, said in November that Japan might respond militarily if China attacked Taiwan. Taiwan is an island that China says is part of its territory. China got very upset and told its citizens not to travel to Japan. It also made it harder for Japanese companies to get rare earth minerals, which are used in electronics.

Now, a group of Japanese politicians from different parties went to China to talk. One of them, Shinichi Isa, said, 'Communication has been severed in all areas.' He said this is the worst the relationship has been since 1972.

China's foreign ministry said some people in Japan are worried and want to help. They hope Japan will listen and work to fix things.

Japan's Prime Minister hasn't changed what she said about Taiwan. But more visits are planned. A former foreign minister will lead another delegation in September, and business leaders will go later.

It's like when friends argue—sometimes you need to talk it out. Will Japan and China become friends again? We'll have to wait and see.
why_it_matters: This shows how disagreements between countries can affect travel and the electronics we use, and why talking things out matters — just like in friendships.

background_read: Japan and China are neighboring countries in Asia, and their relationship affects the whole region.
Beijing (the capital city of China) is where the Japanese lawmakers went for talks.

Taiwan (an island near China that China says is part of its territory) is one of the reasons they disagree, and Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (the head of Japan's government) made a comment about it that upset China.
Article_Structure: WHO: Japanese lawmakers flew to Beijing, and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's earlier statement about Taiwan caused the trouble.
WHAT: Japan and China are trying to fix their relationship after China got upset and limited travel and rare earth minerals.
WHERE: In Beijing, China, where Japanese politicians talked with China's foreign ministry.
WHY: Because 'Communication has been severed in all areas' and the relationship is at its worst since 1972.

perspectives.description: Japan's prime minister still stands by her statement about Taiwan, but Japanese lawmakers want to restart talks.
China was upset about the Taiwan comment and reacted by limiting travel and rare earth minerals, while saying some Japanese people want to help.
More visits are planned in September, including a former foreign minister and business leaders, so both countries are still trying to talk.
